pages.headline: Lakhpati Didi target doubled to 6 crore by March 2029
pages.what: The Centre met the 3 crore Lakhpati Didi milestone a year ahead of the March 2027 target and set a new goal of 6 crore by March 2029. The initiative helps women in self-help groups earn a sustainable household income of about Rs 1 lakh a year.
key: Launched in 2023 under DAY-NRLM, Ministry of Rural Development.
3 crore achieved a year ahead of the March 2027 target.
New target: 6 crore Lakhpati Didis by March 2029.
Needs average monthly income of Rs 10,000 over four seasons or business cycles.
Community Investment Fund support: up to Rs 2.5 lakh per SHG.
pages.static: DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011 as Aajeevika, builds women's self-help groups to raise rural livelihoods.
pages.angle: Trap: it is a Rural Development scheme, not a Women and Child Development one.
pages.remember: Lakhpati Didi: DAY-NRLM, 3 crore done, 6 crore by 2029.

pages.headline: PM Surya Ghar: 30 lakh households get rooftop solar
pages.what: Around 30 lakh households have installed rooftop solar under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, the world's largest domestic rooftop solar initiative. Subsidy rises with plant capacity, up to Rs 78,000 for systems above 3 kW.
key: Free electricity up to 300 units a month for one crore households by 2027.
Central Sector Scheme of MNRE launched in 2024.
About 30 lakh households covered so far.
Subsidy up to Rs 78,000 for plants above 3 kW; loans at around 7 per cent.
Eligibility: valid connection and no other rooftop solar subsidy availed.
pages.static: A Central Sector Scheme is fully funded and implemented by the Union Government, unlike a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
pages.angle: Trap: prior rooftop solar subsidy disqualifies a household.
pages.remember: Surya Ghar: 300 units, one crore homes, MNRE, 2024.

pages.headline: Vibrant Villages Programme-II to develop border villages
pages.when: Launch planned at Cachar, Assam, 20 Feb 2026
pages.what: The Union Home Minister was to launch VVP-II at Cachar district, Assam, to develop border villages in 17 States and Union Territories. It aims at infrastructure, livelihoods through cooperatives and self-help groups and curbing trans-border crime.
key: Central Sector Scheme; outlay Rs 6,839 crore till FY2028-29.
100 per cent Centre-funded.
Border villages in 17 States and Union Territories.
Excludes the northern border covered by VVP-I.
Aims: infrastructure, livelihoods, curbing trans-border crime.
pages.static: The Ministry of Home Affairs implements the Vibrant Villages Programme through its border management department.
pages.angle: Trap: it is fully Centre-funded; there is no State share.
pages.remember: VVP-II: 6,839 crore, 17 States, 100 per cent Centre.

pages.headline: Centre to expand Forest Rights Act cells under DAJGUA
pages.what: The Centre decided to expand Forest Rights Act cells under DAJGUA to speed up recognition of forest rights. The Tribal Affairs Ministry has sanctioned 324 district-level cells in 18 States and Union Territories and 17 State-level cells.
key: 324 district-level FRA cells in 18 States/UTs.
17 State-level cells sanctioned.
DAJGUA launched in October 2024.
FRA, 2006 recognises individual, community and community forest resource rights.
Sanctioned by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
pages.static: The Gram Sabha is the key authority under the Forest Rights Act for verifying claims.
pages.angle: Trap: FRA recognises three types of rights.
pages.remember: DAJGUA: 324 district cells, 18 States; FRA has three rights.

pages.headline: PM-SURAJ portal disburses Rs 1,389.61 crore
pages.what: The PM-SURAJ portal of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment disbursed Rs 1,389.61 crore to 1.39 lakh entrepreneurs from disadvantaged sections in 2024-25. Business loans go up to Rs 15 lakh.
key: Portal of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
Rs 1,389.61 crore disbursed to 1.39 lakh entrepreneurs in 2024-25.
Business loans up to Rs 15 lakh for new businesses.
Routed through NSFDC, NSKFDC and NBCFDC.
Targets entrepreneurs from disadvantaged sections.
pages.static: NSFDC, NSKFDC and NBCFDC are the national finance and development corporations for Scheduled Castes, safai karamcharis and backward classes.
pages.angle: Trap: the loan channels are the three national development corporations.
pages.remember: PM-SURAJ: 1,389.61 crore, 1.39 lakh, up to Rs 15 lakh.

pages.headline: National MSME Council reviews the RAMP programme
pages.what: The fifth meeting of the National MSME Council reviewed RAMP, a World Bank-assisted scheme of the Ministry of MSME. Its sub-schemes are MSME GIFT for green finance, MSE SPICE for the circular economy and MSE ODR for online dispute resolution.
key: RAMP: Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance; World Bank-assisted.
MSME GIFT: green finance.
MSE SPICE: circular economy.
MSE ODR: online dispute resolution for delayed payments.
pages.static: The MSMED Act, 2006 gives micro and small enterprises a right to payment within 45 days.
pages.angle: Trap: ODR is dispute resolution, not credit guarantee.
pages.remember: RAMP: GIFT green, SPICE circular, ODR disputes.

pages.headline: 10.5 lakh civil servants trained under Karmayogi Jan Seva Programme
pages.what: The Capacity Building Commission said 10.5 lakh government servants have been trained under the Rashtriya Karmayogi Large Scale Jan Seva Programme. The programme stresses the values of Seva Bhav and Svadharma.
key: 10.5 lakh government servants trained.
Reported by the Capacity Building Commission.
CBC is the executive body of the Mission Karmayogi framework.
Behavioural transformation initiative for civil servants.
Stresses Seva Bhav and Svadharma.
pages.static: Mission Karmayogi (the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building) was launched in 2020.
pages.angle: Trap: the programme trains government servants, not private staff.
pages.remember: Karmayogi: 10.5 lakh trained; CBC executes.

pages.headline: Budget announces Bharat-VISTAAR, medical hubs and Divyang Kaushal Yojana
pages.what: The Budget announced Bharat-VISTAAR, a multilingual AI tool for farm advisory, a scheme for five regional medical hubs for medical tourism and the Divyang Kaushal Yojana. The health allocation was Rs 1,06,530.42 crore.
key: Bharat-VISTAAR: multilingual AI tool integrating AgriStack for farm advisory.
Scheme for five regional medical hubs for medical tourism.
Health allocation Rs 1,06,530.42 crore, about 10 per cent above revised estimate.
Divyang Kaushal Yojana: customised training for persons with disabilities.
VISTAAR stands for Virtually Integrated System to Access Agricultural Resources.
pages.static: AgriStack gives farmers a unique digital ID linked to land records.
pages.angle: Trap: Divyang means persons with disabilities.
pages.remember: Bharat-VISTAAR farm AI; five medical hubs; Divyang training.

pages.headline: India climbs to 91st in Corruption Perceptions Index 2025
pages.what: Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index 2025 placed India 91st with a score of 39, up from 96th in 2024. Denmark was first with 89, and Somalia and South Sudan scored 9, with Venezuela at 10.
key: India: 91st, score 39 (96th in 2024).
Denmark first with 89, for the eighth time in a row.
Somalia and South Sudan scored 9; Venezuela 10.
Scale: 0 highly corrupt to 100 very clean.
Composite of 3 to 13 surveys; excludes private sector corruption.
pages.static: Transparency International is a Berlin-based non-governmental organisation that publishes the index every year.
pages.angle: Trap: it measures perceived public sector corruption, not experience.
pages.remember: CPI 2025: India 91, score 39; Denmark 89.

pages.headline: India ranks 45th in Network Readiness Index 2025
pages.what: The Portulans Institute's Network Readiness Index 2025 ranked India 45th among 127 economies, up four places, with a score of 54.43. India topped four indicators: telecom investment, AI scientific publications, ICT services exports and e-commerce legislation.
key: Published by the Portulans Institute.
India 45th among 127 economies; up four places.
Score: 54.43 out of 100.
First in four indicators including telecom investment and AI scientific publications.
Also first in ICT services exports and e-commerce legislation.
pages.static: The index scores economies on technology, people, governance and impact pillars.
pages.angle: Trap: the publisher is the Portulans Institute.
pages.remember: NRI: Portulans; India 45 of 127.

pages.headline: UNESCO report 'Bhasha Matters' on mother-tongue education
pages.what: UNESCO's State of the Education Report for India (2025), 'Bhasha Matters: Mother Tongue and Multilingual Education', finds that about 44 per cent of children start school in a language other than the medium of instruction and recommends a National Mission for mother-tongue-based multilingual education.
key: 7th State of the Education Report for India.
Title: Bhasha Matters: Mother Tongue and Multilingual Education.
About 44 per cent start school in a different language than the medium of instruction.
Recommends a National Mission for mother-tongue-based multilingual education.
India's Linguistic Diversity Index is cited as 0.914.
pages.static: The National Education Policy 2020 favours instruction in the mother tongue or home language at least till Grade 5.
pages.angle: Trap: the report favours mother-tongue-based multilingual education.
pages.remember: Bhasha Matters: 44 per cent mismatch; mother-tongue mission.

pages.headline: Gender Budget share rises to 9.37 per cent
pages.what: The share of the Gender Budget in the Union Budget increased to 9.37 per cent, with 53 Ministries/Departments and five Union Territories reporting allocations. Gender budgeting does not create a separate budget; it views the Budget through a gender lens.
key: Share in Union Budget: 9.37 per cent.
53 Ministries/Departments and five UTs reported allocations.
India adopted gender budgeting in 2004-05.
Part A: 100 per cent provision for women; Part B: at least 30 per cent.
Gender Budgeting Scheme sits under the Samarthya sub-scheme of Mission Shakti.
pages.static: Gender budgeting is an accounting lens on existing allocations, not a separate pot of money.
pages.angle: Trap: Part A is 100 per cent; Part B is at least 30 per cent.
pages.remember: Gender Budget 9.37; Part A 100, Part B 30.

pages.headline: NSO to run Survey on Migration from July 2026
pages.what: The National Statistics Office will conduct a Survey on Migration across India from July 2026 to June 2027, capturing the extent and nature of migration, rural-urban and inter-state movement and reasons. PLFS 2020-21 estimated the overall migration rate at 28.9 per cent, far higher for women than men.
key: NSO survey period: July 2026 to June 2027.
Covers extent, nature, rural-urban and inter-state migration, and reasons.
PLFS 2020-21 overall migration rate: 28.9 per cent.
Male migration rate 10.7 per cent; female migration rate 47.9 per cent.
pages.static: The National Statistics Office functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation and also runs the Periodic Labour Force Survey.
pages.angle: Trap: women, not men, show the higher migration rate.
pages.remember: Migration survey July 2026 to June 2027; women 47.9, men 10.7.

pages.headline: Global Gender Gap Report 2025: India slips to 131
pages.what: The WEF Global Gender Gap Report 2025 placed India 131st, down two places from 129th, with the country among the bottom five on the Economic Participation and Opportunity subindex. This put the spotlight on female labour force participation and on the gap between women's STEM degrees and STEM jobs.
key: India ranked 131 in 2025, down from 129 in 2024.
Bottom five on the Economic Participation and Opportunity subindex.
Women are 43 per cent of STEM graduates but about 27 per cent of the STEM workforce.
Goldin's U-curve links women's work to social norms and structural change.
pages.static: The Global Gender Gap Report is published by the World Economic Forum and covers economic participation, education, health and political empowerment.
pages.angle: Trap: women are a minority in India's STEM workforce, not a majority.
pages.remember: WEF gender gap 2025: India 131; STEM women 43 per cent graduates, 27 per cent workforce.

pages.headline: Health Ministry plans nationwide HPV vaccination for 14-year-old girls
pages.what: The Union Health Ministry was set to launch a nationwide HPV vaccination programme for girls aged 14. HPV causes over 95 per cent of cervical cancers, and the vaccine works best when given between the ages of 9 and 26.
key: Nationwide HPV vaccination for girls aged 14.
HPV causes over 95 per cent of cervical cancers.
Vaccine works best between ages 9 and 26.
Launch announced by the Union Health Ministry.
Aims to prevent cervical cancer.
pages.static: Cervical cancer is among the most common cancers in Indian women, and HPV vaccination is a primary prevention tool.
pages.angle: Trap: best between 9 and 26, not after 26.
pages.remember: HPV vaccine: girls aged 14; best 9-26.

pages.headline: Td vaccine to be launched at CRI Kasauli
pages.what: The Union Health Minister was to launch the Tetanus and Adult Diphtheria vaccine at the Central Research Institute, Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh. The vaccine combines purified diphtheria and tetanus toxoids adsorbed on aluminium phosphate.
key: Td vaccine launch at the Central Research Institute, Kasauli.
Combines diphtheria and tetanus toxoids adsorbed on aluminium phosphate.
CRI Kasauli functions under the Directorate General of Health Services.
Protects against tetanus and diphtheria only.
Launched by the Union Health Minister.
pages.static: A toxoid is an inactivated toxin that trains the immune system without causing the disease.
pages.angle: Trap: Td has no pertussis component.
pages.remember: Td = tetanus plus diphtheria toxoids; CRI Kasauli.

pages.headline: FSSAI chicory labelling and CDSCO fast-track approvals
pages.what: FSSAI advised that chicory content be displayed prominently on the front of coffee-powder packs from 1 July. Separately, CDSCO moved to fast-track new-medicine approvals by issuing no-objection certificates for laboratory testing as soon as applications arrive.
key: FSSAI: chicory content on front of coffee-powder packs from 1 July.
FSSAI is a statutory body under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
CDSCO issues NOCs for laboratory testing immediately on receipt of applications.
CDSCO is headed by the Drugs Controller General of India.
CDSCO works under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
pages.static: CDSCO is the national regulator for drugs and medical devices under the Directorate General of Health Services.
pages.angle: Trap: the DCGI, not the Director General of Health Services, heads CDSCO.
pages.remember: FSSAI: 2006 Act, chicory label; CDSCO: DCGI, 1940 Act, fast-track NOC.

pages.headline: TKDL access extended to INPI Brazil
pages.what: The Traditional Knowledge Digital Library signed a cooperation arrangement with INPI Brazil, taking the number of patent offices with TKDL access under non-disclosure agreements to 18. TKDL holds over 5.2 lakh formulations from Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, Sowa Rigpa and Yoga.
key: TKDL set up in 2001 by CSIR and the Ministry of AYUSH.
Cooperation arrangement with INPI Brazil.
18 patent offices have access under non-disclosure agreements.
Over 5.2 lakh formulations from Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, Sowa Rigpa and Yoga.
Available in English, German, French, Japanese and Spanish.
pages.static: TKDL helps prevent bio-piracy by giving patent offices documented prior art on traditional knowledge.
pages.angle: Trap: the languages are foreign languages used by patent examiners.
pages.remember: TKDL: 2001, 18 offices, five foreign languages.

pages.headline: Centenary of the Ol Chiki script inaugurated
pages.what: President Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the centenary celebrations of the Ol Chiki script. Developed by Raghunath Murmu in 1925, it moved Santhali from an oral to a written tradition after earlier use of Roman, Bengali, Odia and Devanagari scripts.
key: Ol Chiki developed in 1925 by Raghunath Murmu.
Made for the Santhali language.
Santhali: Austroasiatic family; in the Eighth Schedule via the 92nd Amendment, 2003.
Earlier written in Roman, Bengali, Odia and Devanagari.
Santhali spoken in Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Assam and Bihar.
pages.static: The 92nd Amendment, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule, raising its languages to 22.
pages.angle: Trap: Santhali is Austroasiatic, not Dravidian.
pages.remember: Ol Chiki: 1925, Murmu, Santhali, 92nd Amendment.

pages.headline: Tamil Brahmi inscriptions found in the Valley of the Kings
pages.what: Researchers identified close to 30 inscriptions in Tamil Brahmi, Prakrit and Sanskrit at tombs in Egypt's Valley of the Kings, dating to the 1st and 3rd centuries CE. They name traders such as Cikai Korran and shed light on ancient trade links.
key: About 30 inscriptions in Tamil Brahmi, Prakrit and Sanskrit.
Belong to the 1st and 3rd centuries CE.
Names of traders such as Cikai Korran appear.
Valley of the Kings: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
Holds tombs of 18th to 20th dynasty pharaohs.
pages.static: Sangam literature mentions Roman trade through Muziris and other ports on the Tamil coast.
pages.angle: Trap: the dating is CE, not BCE.
pages.remember: Tamil Brahmi in Egypt: 1st-3rd centuries CE.

pages.headline: Wajid Ali Shah, the Nawab who revived Kathak
pages.what: Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of Awadh, ascended in 1847, was removed when the British annexed Awadh in 1856 and is credited with reviving Kathak. He built the Qaiserbagh Palace Complex and wrote the Urdu autobiography Ishqnamah.
key: Last Nawab of Awadh; ascended 1847.
Awadh annexed by the British in 1856.
Credited with reviving Kathak.
Qaiserbagh Palace Complex built 1848-50.
Urdu autobiography: Ishqnamah; died at Metiabruz, Kolkata.
pages.static: Awadh was annexed under the pretext of misgovernance, and its annexation fed discontent that surfaced in the Revolt of 1857.
pages.angle: Trap: Ishqnamah is in Urdu.
pages.remember: Wajid Ali Shah: Awadh 1847-56, Kathak, Urdu Ishqnamah.

pages.headline: Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti: Father of the Indian Navy
pages.what: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, born at Shivneri Fort near Pune on 19 February 1630, pursued Hindavi Swarajya. He is called the Father of the Indian Navy for building a fleet and coastal forts such as Sindhudurg.
key: Born 19 February 1630 at Shivneri Fort near Pune.
Called Father of the Indian Navy.
Built a fleet and coastal forts such as Sindhudurg.
Pursued Hindavi Swarajya.
Used Marathi and Sanskrit in administration instead of Persian.
pages.static: Sindhudurg is a sea fort on an island off the Konkan coast of Maharashtra.
pages.angle: Trap: Persian was replaced, not introduced.
pages.remember: Shivaji: 1630, Shivneri, Navy father, Marathi over Persian.

pages.headline: Bharat GI unveiled; Salem Sago exported to Canada
pages.what: DPIIT unveiled Bharat GI, a national umbrella initiative to showcase India's GI products. APEDA facilitated the first export of 0.5 MT of GI-tagged Salem Sago from Tamil Nadu to Canada.
key: Bharat GI: DPIIT initiative for global showcasing of GI products.
Unveiled at the India AI Impact Summit.
Salem Sago (Javvarisi): made from tapioca starch; GI tag in 2023.
First export of 0.5 MT to Canada facilitated by APEDA.
APEDA works under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
pages.static: GI tags are granted under the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999.
pages.angle: Trap: APEDA, not DGFT, facilitated the export.
pages.remember: Bharat GI = DPIIT; Salem Sago via APEDA.

pages.headline: Milano Cortina 2026: Norway tops medal table
pages.what: The XXV Winter Olympics opened on 6 February 2026 at San Siro, Milan, and ended on 22 February. Norway topped the medal table with 18 golds, and Johannes Hoesflot Klaebo won six golds, a first for a Winter Olympian at one Games.
key: Opened 6 February 2026 at San Siro, Milan; closed 22 February at Verona Arena.
Norway 18 golds; United States 12; Netherlands 10.
Johannes Hoesflot Klaebo won six golds, a first at a single Games.
India sent two athletes and won no medals.
Arif Khan finished 39th in the men's slalom.
pages.static: India has never won a Winter Olympic medal.
pages.angle: Trap: the Verona Arena hosted the closing, not the opening.
pages.remember: Norway 18 golds; India no medal; open San Siro, close Verona.

pages.headline: Grammys and BAFTAs 2026: Bad Bunny and One Battle After Another
pages.what: At the 68th Grammy Awards on 1 February, Bad Bunny won Album of the Year, the first primarily Spanish-language album to do so, and Kendrick Lamar won five awards. At the 79th BAFTAs on 22 February, One Battle After Another won six awards including Best Film.
key: 68th Grammys, 1 February 2026: Bad Bunny won Album of the Year.
First primarily Spanish-language album to win Album of the Year.
Kendrick Lamar won five awards, including Record of the Year.
Olivia Dean won Best New Artist.
79th BAFTAs: One Battle After Another won six awards; Sinners won three.
pages.static: The BAFTA Film Awards are given by the British Academy of Film and Television Arts, and the Grammys by the Recording Academy of the United States.
pages.angle: Trap: One Battle After Another, not Sinners, won Best Film.
pages.remember: Grammys: Bad Bunny; BAFTA 2026: One Battle After Another, six awards.
